subject: astronaut sandwich
title: What If You Smuggled a Sandwich Into Space? In 1965 It Reached Congress

scenes.text: What if you smuggled a sandwich into orbit? In 1965 an astronaut did, and Congress got involved.
March 23, 1965. Gemini 3 lifts off with Gus Grissom and John Young, and a corned beef sandwich hidden in Young's spacesuit pocket.
In orbit, Young hands it over. Grissom takes one bite, and within about ten seconds the bread is breaking up.
In weightlessness, crumbs don't fall. They can drift behind electrical panels, or into an astronaut's eyes and lungs.
The flight lasted under five hours. Back on Earth, Congress grilled NASA over what it called a 30 million dollar sandwich.
NASA promised to prevent any recurrence of corned beef sandwiches. Then, in 1981, corned beef flew again, officially, on the first space shuttle. Its commander: John Young.

description:
What if you smuggled a sandwich into space? On Gemini 3, launched 23 March 1965, pilot John Young pulled a corned beef sandwich from his spacesuit pocket and handed it to commander Gus Grissom, who took one bite before it started to crumble.
Floating crumbs can get behind electrical panels or into eyes and lungs, and the stunt came up in Congress, where it was called a 30 million dollar sandwich; NASA said it had taken steps to prevent a recurrence. Corned beef flew officially on Young's first shuttle flight in 1981.
